data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise the Past Perfect to show that one past event happened before another past event.
data.learningTitle: Ordering Past Events with the Past Perfect
learningPoints: Use had + past participle to form the Past Perfect.
Use the tense for an earlier past event before another past event.
Use the Past Simple for the later event in a sequence.
Use already, just and never naturally with the Past Perfect.
Recognise when chronological order is already clear.
Avoid using the Past Perfect when only one simple past event is needed.

sections.explain: Use HAD + past participle for the earlier of two past events.

words.word: When I arrived, the film had already started.
When I had arrived, the film already started.
When I arrived, the film has already started.

sections.summary: Using Past Perfect before Past Simple.
sections.explain: The Past Perfect marks the earlier event; the Past Simple often marks the later event.

words.word: She had left before I called.
She has left before I called.
She had leave before I called.

sections.explain: GO has the past participle GONE after HAD.

words.word: They had gone home by the time we arrived.
They had went home by the time we arrived.
They have gone home by the time we arrived.

sections.explain: Use HAD NEVER + past participle for something that had not happened before a past moment.

words.word: I had never flown before that trip.
I never had flew before that trip.
I had never flew before that trip.

sections.explain: JUST can show that one event happened shortly before another past event.

words.word: We had just sat down when the lights went out.
We just had sat down when the lights went out.
We had just sit down when the lights went out.

sections.explain: The Past Perfect can explain the earlier cause of a past situation.

words.word: He was tired because he had slept badly.
He was tired because he has slept badly.
He was tired because he had sleep badly.

sections.explain: BY THE TIME often introduces the later past point, with the earlier action in the Past Perfect.

words.word: By the time we got there, the shop had closed.
By the time we had got there, the shop closed before.
By the time we got there, the shop has closed.

sections.explain: If events are simply listed in chronological order, the Past Simple is often enough.

words.word: I got up, had breakfast and left the house.
I had got up, had had breakfast and had left the house.
I have got up, had breakfast and left the house.

sections.explain: Use HADN'T + past participle for an earlier event that did not happen.

words.word: She hadn't seen the message before the meeting.
She didn't had seen the message before the meeting.
She hadn't saw the message before the meeting.

sections.explain: Use HAD + subject + past participle in a question.

words.word: Had you met him before the party?
Did you had met him before the party?
Had you metted him before the party?
